deep.reconstruction:
Setting (q = x, everything as power series). Ramanujan defines two weight-8 cusp forms of level 9:
 F(x) = x^2 prod_{k>=1}(1-x^{3k})^16 = eta(3tau)^16 = sum a_n x^n.
 F_1(x) = x prod_{k>=1}(1-x^{3k})^8 * (1 + 240 sum_{m>=1} m^3 x^{3m}/(1-x^{3m})) = eta(3tau)^8 E_4(3tau) = sum A_n x^n.
F is supported on n ≡ 2 (mod 3) and F_1 on n ≡ 1 (mod 3).

Claim. The combinations f_± = F_1 ± 6√10 F have Euler products of Hecke type for weight k = 8 with trivial character:
 sum (A_n ± 6√10 a_n) n^{-s} = prod_{p≠3} 1/(1 - c_±(p) p^{-s} + p^{7-2s}).
The stated Euler factors are:
 p=2: c_+(2) = 6√10.
 p=5: c_+(5) = -96√10.
 p=7: c_+(7) = 260.
 p=11: c_+(11) = -1920√10.
For f_- the signs flip at p = 2, 5, 11 (all p ≡ 2 mod 3) but not at p = 7 (p ≡ 1 mod 3). There is no factor at p = 3, since all coefficients with 3 | n vanish.

Verification of the coefficients (my computation; Ramanujan shows none of it). Write y = x^3.
 prod(1-y^k)^8 = 1 - 8y + 20y^2 + 0y^3 - 70y^4 + ...
 E_4 = 1 + 240y + 2160y^2 + 6720y^3 + ...
 Product: 1 + 232y + 260y^2 - 5760y^3 + ...
 So A_1 = 1, A_4 = 232, A_7 = 260, A_10 = -5760.
 prod(1-y^k)^16 = 1 - 16y + 104y^2 - 320y^3 + ...
 So a_2 = 1, a_5 = -16, a_8 = 104, a_11 = -320.
Hence:
 c(2) = 6√10·a_2 = 6√10.
 c(5) = 6√10·(-16) = -96√10.
 c(7) = A_7 = 260.
 c(11) = 6√10·(-320) = -1920√10.
All match the page.

Hecke-relation consistency checks (mine):
 c(4) = c(2)^2 - 2^7 = 360 - 128 = 232 = A_4.
 c(8) = c(2)(c(4) - 2^7) = 6√10·104 = 6√10·a_8.
 c(10) = c(2)c(5) = -5760 = A_10.
So the normalization 6√10 is exactly what makes F_1 ± 6√10 F eigenforms. Note c(2)^2 = 360 is forced by A_4 = 232 = c(2)^2 - 128.

Interpretation. f_+ and f_- are the two Galois-conjugate newforms in S_8^new(Γ0(9)) with coefficient field Q(√10). Conjugation agrees with twisting by the character (−3/·), giving an inner twist. That explains why c(p) is rational for p ≡ 1 (mod 3) and lies in √10·Q for p ≡ 2 (mod 3).

The page continues the previous folio. There Ramanujan treated eta(4tau)^18, a form with an analogous splitting, and listed further eta-powers expected to behave the same way.
errors: No mathematical errors found: the Euler factors at p=2,5,7,11 and the sign pattern in the conjugate product all check against the q-expansions.
The page is an unproved statement. Multiplicativity is asserted from numerical evidence (implicit); the general proof requires Hecke operators (Hecke 1937).
The final '+11^{7-2s}' in the second product has an overwritten exponent, but it is clearly 7-2s.

results.what: Euler product for the Dirichlet series of eta(3τ)^8E_4(3τ) ± 6√10 eta(3τ)^16, with factors (1 - c(p)p^{-s} + p^{7-2s})^{-1} and c(2)=±6√10, c(5)=∓96√10, c(7)=260, c(11)=∓1920√10
results.modern_name: Hecke eigenforms (newform orbit with coefficient field Q(√10)) in S_8(Γ0(9)); Hecke theory of Euler products; inner twist by χ_{-3}
results.usually_credited_to: Mordell (1917) for Δ-type multiplicativity; Hecke (1937) for general theory; Petersson for eigenbasis

results.what: Recognition that coefficients p≡1 mod 3 are rational and p≡2 mod 3 lie in √10·Q, with conjugate form obtained by sign change at p≡2 mod 3
results.modern_name: Inner twist / Galois conjugation equals twist by quadratic character mod 3
results.usually_credited_to: Ribet, Momose (1980s) for general theory of inner twists

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit pre-Hecke example of Euler products for eigenforms with irrational (real quadratic) Hecke eigenvalues. The pair is found as specific linear combinations of eta products, with the inner-twist pattern visible. It is notable, but Ramanujan's Euler-product fragments from these manuscripts have been published and discussed (e.g. in the Andrews–Berndt Lost Notebook volumes), so it is likely already partly known as his.

checkable.sympy: x=symbols('x'); N=40; P=prod([(1-x**(3*k)) for k in range(1,15)]); F=series(x**2*P**16,x,0,N).removeO(); F1=series(x*P**8*(1+240*sum(m**3*x**(3*m)/(1-x**(3*m)) for m in range(1,15))),x,0,N).removeO(); [F1.coeff(x,n) for n in (1,4,7,10,13)], [F.coeff(x,n) for n in (2,5,8,11)]
